evidence: Ter. Ph. 1052–1053: vīn' prīmum hodiē facere quod ego gaudeam …? — Cupiō.
Plaut. Mil. 535: Vīn' scīre plānē? — Cupiō.
terms.comment: The comic answer to an offer put with vīn': “Would you like …?” “I’d love to.” Latin answers with a verb, not with a word for yes; so also Volō, which repeats the verb of the question. Amābō and sīs go with a request of one’s own (see “please”).

evidence: Plaut. Amph. 769: Vīn' prōferrī pateram? — Prōferrī volō.

phrases.latin: vīn' prīmum hodiē facere quod ego gaudeam … et quod tuō virō oculī doleant? — Cupiō. — Mē ad cēnam vocā.
phrases.english: Would you like, first of all, to do something today that will make me happy … and make your husband’s eyes sore? — I’d love to. — Invite me to dinner.
Do you want to know for sure? — Yes, please.
Do you want the bowl brought out? — Yes, I do.
Would you like more milk? — Yes, please!

sources: Lewis & Short: cupio · Lewis & Short: volo
